messages.subject: Proposal: always exclude */inst/doc/*.html from our team-maintained r-cran- and r-bioc- packages.
messages.subject_clean: Proposal: always exclude */inst/doc/*.html from our team-maintained r-cran- and r-bioc- packages.
messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody,

at the moment we are removing HTML files containing minified Javascript from
the r-cran- and r-bioc- source packages using the Files-Excluded field in
debian/copyright for `*/inst/doc/*.html` and the repack capacity of uscan.
This is more or less on a case-by-case basis, which requires the attention of
maintainers, team uploaders and reviewers.

To save people time, which is essential given how many packages we have, I
propose to make this systematic.  The main drawback is that some Free HTML
files with no minified Javascript code may be deleted as well.  On my side, I
think that it is not a problem since 1) we still ship their source, and 2)
they are still available on the Upstream sites.

For the implementation, we would default new packages and update old packages
to have a `Files-Excluded` field containing at least `*/inst/doc/*.html`, and
switch the watch files to uscan format version 5 using new CRAN and
Bioconductor templates that I am preparing here:

https://salsa.debian.org/debian/devscripts/-/merge_requests/618/diffs

Please let me know your thoughts.

Charles 

--

Hi Michael,

we can easily replace the contents of the Files-Excluded field with a command like:

    cme modify dpkg-copyright 'Files-Excluded="foo"'

I have not found a tool to extract the current value, but in worst case it
should be easy to parse.

> The template is a good idea, but unrelated to excluding the HTML files, yes?

We need to update the watch files so that the +dfsg suffix is added in case of
repacking.  Using the templates, we can just fix all watch files to the same
standard.

> Also, I guess there is no habit of rendering the docs in r-* packages?

There are a couple of cases in r-bioc-*, but otherwise it is not mainstream.  Maybe
this is something we can consider in the future.

Cheers,

Hi Paul,

On 10 February 2026 at 20:00, Paul Gevers wrote:
| Source: rcpp
| Version: 1.1.0-1
| Severity: serious

| Tags: sid forky
| User: release.debian.org at packages.debian.org
| Usertags: out-of-sync
| 
| Dear maintainer(s),
| 
| The Release Team considers packages that are out-of-sync between testing 
| and unstable for more than 30 days as having a Release Critical bug in 
| testing [1]. Your package src:rcpp has been trying to migrate for 31 
| days [2], hence this bug report. The current output of the migration 
| software for this package is copied to the bottom of this report and 
| should list the reason why the package is blocked.
| 
| If a package is out of sync between unstable and testing for a longer 
| period, this usually means that bugs in the package in testing cannot be 
| fixed via unstable. Additionally, blocked packages can have impact on 
| other packages, which makes preparing for the release more difficult. 
| Finally, it often exposes issues with the package and/or its 
| (reverse-)dependencies. We expect maintainers to fix issues that hamper 
| the migration of their package in a timely manner.
| 
| This bug will trigger auto-removal when appropriate. As with all new 
| bugs, there will be at least 30 days before the package is auto-removed.
| 
| This bug submission immediately closes the bug with the version in 
| unstable, so if that version or a later version migrates, this bug will 
| no longer affect testing. This bug is also tagged to only affect sid and 
| forky, so it doesn't affect (old-)stable.
| 
| If you believe your package is unable to migrate to testing due to 
| issues beyond your control, don't hesitate to contact the Release Team.

This is downstream from me.

Looking at the error I see for (r-cran-)phylobase at e.g.g amd64 that

  > library('phylobase')
  Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘phylobase’:
   object ‘loadRcppModules’ is not exported by 'namespace:Rcpp'
  Execution halted

so that is an error in the package's autpkgtest.

Rcpp (for which I happen to be upstream) no longer exports loadRcppModules
because it is a form of using Rcpp Modules that has been superceded for a
decade (!!) -- see

  https://github.com/RcppCore/Rcpp/issues/1415
  https://github.com/RcppCore/Rcpp/pull/1416

for more.

It is the same issue with (r-cran-)rncl.

I am cc'ing debian-r, hopefully someone from the Debian R Packager team wants
to take care of this.  (I can point to different Rcpp Modules resources if
need be.)

Cheers, Dirk

Yes indeed, it is an issue in r-cran-rncl 0.8.7-1 in Testing, which I
fixed in Unstable by upgrading to 0.8.9-1 two weeks ago.

r-cran-rncl 0.8.9-1 will not migrate to Testing untill all of its
reverse dependencies (transitively) have completed the transition to the
removal of non-64-bit non-little-endian architectures, which I hope to
complete befrore the end of March but I can not promise that for sure.

r-cran-rncl 0.8.7-1 will be automatically removed from Testing on March
8th because of the namespace issue above (#1126238).  After that,
r-cran-rcpp can migrate to Testing because it will not break r-cran-rncl
anymore.

If there were a system empowering me to remove r-cran-rncl from the way,
I would surely use it, but I am not aware of such a tool.

Paul, could you place a hint that does what is needed for r-cran-rcpp
to migrate earlier than March 8th?

I really feel sorry that the current situation strains a lot of time
from all the parties but once the vast majority of the r-cran-* packages
are built only on supported architectures, there will me much less
migration bottlenecks like this one.

Have a nie day,

Charles

Hi again,

if I submit a patch to devscripts, we can use information already existing in
debian/upstream/metadata and get rid of debian/watch entirely, once the
devscript package containing defaults for CRAN and Bioconductor lands in
Testing!  This makes us one step closer to full automation of CRAN/Bioc package
maintainance.

Our dh-make|update-R scripts already place the appropriate `Archive` field
with the values of either CRAN or Bioconductor.  Remains the package upstream
name.

One devscripts d/u/metadata-to-watch translator (CPAN) uses Upstream-Name
despate DEP12 saying that it should not be there.

The other (GitHub) uses Repository or Repository-Name.

I would like to use the d/u/metadata route.  What should we use for the package name?

 - Package
 - Package-Name
 - Upstream-Name
 - Upstream-Name but grep it from debian/copyright
 - something else?

Have a nice day,

Charles

Hi Dirk,

thanks again for your patience.  The migration to remove non-supported
architectures is progressing well and today I finally managed to produce
some code that I needed to write "dak rm" commands for removal requests.

https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/maintenance-utilities/-/blob/master/rdeps.R?ref_type=heads

Thank you for sharing earlier with me some code to parse dependencies, but I
needed something that was more transitive and that also included
Build-Depdends.

I went ahead and asked for the removal (https://bugs.debian.org/1128383) of
r-cran-ade4 and its reverse dependencies (phylobase, ...) in the unsupported
architectures, which should allow their migration and therefore stop blocking
rcpp.

Next I will check about rncl.

Once we have the unsupported architectures removed broady I expect the r-cran-*
package ecosystem to be much more stable and much easier to keep up to date.

We still build on more architectures than CRAN and, although it is rare, the
autopkgtests also uncover real issues.  For instance we had one case where the
CRAN package was expecting characters to be signed like on Mac, but on Linux
ARM64 they are unsigned.

Have a nice day,

Charles

Hi Paul,

I finished today to write some R code that parses Debian's dependency
graph to help me check that if I ask for a recursive removal to the the
Archive time, the 32-bit/big-endian buildds are not going to replace the
binaries immediately.  (That is, that the whole subgraph went through
the architecture restriction).

https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/maintenance-utilities/-/blob/master/rdeps.R?ref_type=heads

I am making a small-scale test with https://bugs.debian.org/1128383,
and will ramp up it it worked well.

I hope that we are seeing the light at the end of the tunnel, although
I worry that the architecture-independant packages will cause a problem
that I did not foresee when I started this project.

Have a nice day,

Charles
